Mr. Scott, you wanted to take the floor because I was under the impression that there was an exchange, perhaps a misunderstanding. So you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Your Honour, first of all, it shouldn't be the Prosecution that's being accused of using this language. This is evidence that was contemporaneously produced in 1993. The Prosecution doesn't select what words somebody used in 1993 anyway -- any more than we use -- select any other offensive language that might show up in a number of documents. Further just in quick response to Mr. Karnavas, yes, I did object to some of the things that Mr. Praljak was doing and my objection was overruled. So unless there again is one set of rules for the Prosecution and a different set of rules for the Defence, I think I should be allowed to ask the question, and that follows on again that that follows from the very cross-examination put by Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And, sir, the language that you've now seen and heard discussed in the last couple of minutes, can you make further comment on that in light of the answer you gave to us a few moments ago?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, again I'm going to object and here is a different reason: There has been no testimony from this particular gentleman, and I'm now speaking about at least one of the accused, Mr. Stojic, that there was an observation from this particular gentleman that Mr. Stojic was characterised in any way as being a paranoid or extremist or that he was -- and he didn't hide these qualities. I think he's being asked to speculate about what somebody else might have believed or observed or thought of. Now, if they wish to elicit this sort of testimony, then I suggest they bring this particular gentleman here and then we can have access to the cross-examination of that gentleman. So again not only is this improper but it also violates the rights of confrontation that are enshrined in Article 20 and 21 of the -- of the ICTY Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm -- I'm -- frankly I'm astounded. I'm astounded by these objections in light of everything that I've heard from the Defence in the last six or seven hours, and the nature of the questions that were put to this witness, and the opinions that were asked of him on any wide range of topics. This is no different whatsoever. And again, unless we have two sets of rules in this courtroom then I believe I should be able to answer -- ask the question. The witness should be able to finish his testimony by giving us his observation on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Technically speaking, when we have a criminal case we have a document, the author of this document is not present. This document was given to -- shown to the witness. The witness was -- part of the same department of the same service where this person, the author of the person [as interpreted] was, and in this document four people are mentioned, Boban, Stojic, Kordic, and Valentin [as interpreted]. It was not something that the witness said. It is something that the witness -- that the author of the document said, and the witness told us that he met those people at the time, some people, some important people. I remember that he mentioned Valenta.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Not Valentin but Valenta.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the Prosecutor can ask the witness those questions because he can put the question to the witness and say: This is what was said at the time. Do you agree or disagree with this, and then the Judges of this Chamber will see what -- will debate on this or will be able to conclude. You may proceed, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Watkins, I don't think I have to repeat the matters further to you. Do you have any comment or observations you can make in concluding your testimony on this?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I directly met and knew well Mr. Kordic, Mr. Valenta, and Mr. Boban. We've established that I met Mr. Stojic but not well. In the case of the three that I do know, I would describe them as the ideological voice of the Bosnian Croat community. And in the case -- in each case taking something of what I would describe broadly as a more extreme view of solutions to the fighting and the political structures of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And this is a particular reference and -- to Mr. Valenta and his maps. We've heard the origin of those maps, which I didn't know, but one only had to meet Mr. Valenta to hear him describing these movements of population and seeing them as desirable solutions to the fighting in -- or the situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina. And it wasn't one where the future was being embraced in the legitimate, internationally recognised bodies. It was about a new order, a separation, and part of that separation was creating a geographical physical area which has a boundary and collecting in that the Croat people. It was very clear to me that that was an aim of Mr. Valenta, and my impression would be also of Mr. Kordic and Mr. Boban that that was what they were trying to achieve.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Watkins, on behalf of the Prosecution I'd like to thank you once again for coming to The Hague and giving your testimony. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to make a motion that the -- at some time convenient to the Trial Chamber Mr. Watkins be recalled for further cross-examination by Mr. Stojic. We have been ambushed by this testimony. It's completely illegitimate and I'm entitled, I think, to cross-examine as to the basis of this opinion that he has expressed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Murphy, the witness just stated there were four people. He talked about the three people that he knew well, but he didn't really say anything about Mr. Stojic. He didn't say anything. He talked about the three other people, and he just said that he had met Mr. Stojic but he did not include your client in the group of the three other people, unless you understood differently. But this is what I understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand that you can get up and make objections, but you have to listen to what the witness has stated. The Prosecutor talked to him about four people. He said there are four people in this paragraph. "What is your comment?" And the witness said, "I met those four people," but he only talked about the three. He did not say anything about your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: If I have the Trial Chamber's assurance that's their understanding, then, of course, I'm -- I'm content with that, but the fact is that if there is any doubt about that, because Mr. Scott could easily have avoided that line of re-examination that did not arise from anything that was said in direct or by cross-examination by Mr. Stojic, then we are entitled --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The doubt will be lifted immediately. I will put the question to the witness. Witness, you just heard this exchange. The Prosecutor asked you to make some comments on this paragraph where it is -- where Mr. Boban, Mr. Stojic, Mr. Valenta are mentioned. The author of the document is not yourself. It is Mr. Thebault. And Mr. Thebault, therefore, the author of this document, says that there are various situations on various topics. He talked about the paranoia, the extremism. The Prosecutor wanted you to know what you think of it, and you said, "I met Boban, Stojic, Kordic, and Valenta." And then you stated, regarding Valenta, Boban, and Kordic, you said what you said about them. And then with regard to Mr. Stojic, you mention that you only met him once, but I was not under the impression that you put him in the group, that you include him in that group. So could you please state your thoughts on this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, your interpretation is exactly correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This is what I thought so -- as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, just very briefly because the record has been made, let me also be very clear about the record, and I've just gone back in the transcript. Today at page 46, line 17, Mr. Praljak put exactly this document and this section of the document to the witness and asked him about that, and I -- the one reason -- the reason I came back to the document, in fact, is because in my observation Mr. Watkins was attempting to go give a fuller answer to it, and at one point he was cut off by Mr. Praljak. It's on page -- it's on page 46 and that was completely within cross-examination and completely appropriate for redirect to give Mr. Watkins a chance to give a full answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's slightly disingenuous because -- because the latter part that has just been brought up by the Prosecution, they could have done that on direct examination, first and foremost. Secondly, Mr. Praljak was not addressing whether somebody was Balkan or whether they suffer from paranoia or extremism. That was something that the Prosecution decided to bring on in redirect and it is -- it's improper. It is not your classic redirect based on the cross-examination. Obviously, they had every right to ask for fuller answer to a question that was cut off, to an answer that was cut off during cross-examination, but then they went beyond the pale. But in any event, the document speaks for itself. It's -- it's in the evidence and the Judges can draw whatever conclusion. And since we don't have this gentleman here, I suggest that little or no weight be given to the document until the gentleman comes here so he can be thoroughly cross-examined.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission, might I be allowed to say something? I'd just like to give a brief explanation and ask your indulgence for me to ask two or three questions with respect to this document, because I want to make it quite clear to the Trial Chamber that this document was something that the Prosecution didn't use in the examination-in-chief, and for that reason some of the observations made, which do not refer to any qualifications but to events, what happened at that time in Kakanj and Travnik and those events can, in a way, overthrow those qualifications, and for that I had prepared to ask this witness something, but as the Prosecutor failed to show the document and present it during in chief, it was only Mr. Praljak who brought did up in the cross-examination. And the Prosecution has referred to it. I would like to ask you if I might have a few moments to ask the witness something more. The witness was in the area mentioned in the document, and it is Travnik, and the area around Travnik, so may I be allowed to ask him a few questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica, no. The Prosecution only mentioned this famous paragraph with Kordic, Valenta, Stojic, and Boban. Nothing else was mentioned by the Prosecution during the re-examination. Furthermore, I am under the impression that we'll have the opportunity to look at this document again at length, it seems to me. Now we have to conclude. Witness, on behalf of my fellow Judges I would like to thank you -- yes, Mr. Praljak. Mr. Praljak, I hate being interrupted. I think that everything has been said. What do you want to add?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. In view of the fact that my learned colleague Mr. Scott asked redirect question with respect to the chain of command, although my questions were not linked to the chain of command but exclusively to the subject of authorities for appointing and replacing individual commanders of their duty, I consider that with this witness, who has very good knowledge about the events on the ground, it would be a good idea to clarify three additional questions. So may I be allowed to do so? It will only last a half a minute, and you can see for yourself whether you consider it important or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll have other witnesses, more qualified witnesses who will talk to us about the chain of command. No. We would just be wasting time. Mr. Praljak --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour. Your Honour, I would just like to ask for half a minute just to have these questions of mine recorded. You needn't allow for them to be answered, but this witness said that the Supreme Commander, in the month of October 1993, was Mr. Praljak, and we all know that that's not true, and I think that we ought to give the witness a chance to say who in fact was the Supreme Commander of the armed force of Herceg-Bosna. That's the first point. Secondly, the witness said that on the basis of a conversation he had with Colonel Blaskic about the fact that he defined Petkovic as his superior, one could conclude that Petkovic was more or less the sole superior officer. And I think it's relevant to ask him: Does that mean that Mr. Blaskic denied the superiority of the Supreme Command of the commander of the HVO. And the third very important question and the witness spoke about this at length in the Blaskic trial is the -- a question linked to the possibility of communication, control, and command on the territory of Central Bosnia for which reason, according to his words, if I have interpreted them correctly, Colonel Blaskic was the person who referred to or reported to Dario Kordic, and Dario Kordic was the person who de facto had control over events in Central Bosnia, and I think that this witness has a lot of knowledge on ALL these questions and that his answers would contribute to a better understanding of the facts in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We've taken good note of your statement. Mr. Praljak, I just wanted to tell you that I didn't want to interrupt you, but for me we had come to a conclusion here. I don't want you to have the feeling that we don't want to listen to you, but what did you want to say when you stood up?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I didn't want to do anything special. All I wanted to say was that I think that Mr. Watkins is an objective person, but I wanted to show by use of documents to show that unfortunately they do not -- did not possess the kind -- the information that was commensurate to the situation. So you can be objective, but if you don't have the necessary information you can't interpret a situation. So I don't want you to misunderstand me and think that I said that he was unobjective, an unobjective observer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Thank you very much. As I was saying, thank you very much, Witness. On behalf of my fellow Judges, thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for testifying throughout the week. I'm going to ask the usher to escort you out the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, let's talk about next week. As you know, we have a bank holiday. Therefore, we'll only resume the proceedings on Tuesday. We'll be sitting in the afternoon. We have a witness scheduled. The examination in chief is scheduled to take five hours. At this stage we have decided to grant six hours for cross-examination. The time should normally be divided equally amongst the Defence team, subject of course to review made -- that the Trial Chamber will make on Tuesday morning. So we might reconsider that. But theoretically each and -- each Defence team should have one hour, and it's up to you, of course, to divide and spread the time amongst yourselves as you see fit, what you've done when this particular witness. So if I'm not mistaken, Mr. Scott, next week we have one witness to be heard by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Scott, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me. Your Honour, if we might go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We are in open session. The proceedings will resume on Tuesday at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 29th day of May, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.41 p.m.,
